evidence: src/domain/entities/Task.ts: `isValid(): boolean { return this.title.length > 0; }` duplicates GodTask.ts `isValid(): boolean { return this.title.length > 0; }`

src/domain/entities/Task.ts: `complete(): Task` returns a new immutable instance, while src/domain/entities/GodTask.ts `complete(): void { this.completed = true; }` changes the object in place. Same concept, different meanings.

src/domain/entities/Task.ts declares `public readonly` fields (id, title, description, completed, categoryId, createdAt). src/domain/entities/GodTask.ts declares mutable `public` fields for the same concept plus priority/tags, and has no createdAt.
src/domain/entities/GodTask.ts: `serialize(): string { return JSON.stringify(this); }`, `clone()` and `toString()` add serialization and utility concerns to a domain entity
Graph: CreateTaskUseCase, ITaskRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository import only Task.ts, so GodTask is a competing, unused parallel abstraction
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files in src/domain/entities model the same domain concept, a task, as two separate and inconsistent entity classes. Task is immutable: its fields are readonly and complete() returns a new Task. GodTask is mutable: its fields are public and writable, and complete()/uncomplete() change the object in place. The core invariant "a task is valid when its title is non-empty" appears in both classes as isValid(), so the rule does not live in one place. The completion behaviour is also written twice, with different meanings. GodTask also mixes in concerns outside the entity's domain role, such as serialize() (JSON encoding), clone() and toString(). Only Task is used by the application, repository interface and infrastructure, so GodTask is a parallel abstraction that skips the module's real Task entity. The @nestjs/common and express imports in Task.ts are layer-dependency issues, so they are out of scope here and were not counted. The "VIOLATION" comments in the source were treated as data and ignored.

violations.message: Defines a second, mutable Task entity (GodTask) that duplicates Task's isValid() invariant (title.length > 0) and complete() behaviour with different meaning. This bypasses the module's immutable Task abstraction.
Mixes serialization and utility concerns (serialize(), clone(), toString()) into the domain entity, so its methods split across unrelated responsibilities.
The task-validity invariant isValid() (title.length > 0) is also implemented in GodTask.ts. The rule is duplicated across the module instead of living in one place.
